title: Buck's boogie and disliking their part
summary: He praises Buck making classics swing and says producers just wanted names, so he disliked the entrance and role.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: That's the same way with this "Aneetra" s(?) Boogie" on the piano Buck had played, sextet from "di Lammemoor." He played "William Tell," he'd play any kind of piece you'd think about on the piano and make it ragtime, swing -- you knew all the a, b, and these people, long-haired musicians and they want to learn what the jazz is all about. So he only had a chance to play "Aneetra" s like) Boogie" once and he could swing it. I know you heard it before so you know what it goes like. And he did a good job. But the idea was we didn't have much to do in the picdure, not much. The idea was I guess he wanted a name, like Lionel Hampton and Walter Catlett and a couple of other fellas in there that was known. He wants the names in the thing and put on any old thing. It was a good play for as they're concerned, but I didn't think

much of it. I didn't like our entrance. I didn't like our part in it at all. So many things I don't like about certain things in pictures that they do. I just go along with it, that's all. They contract you for it and I can do it, it's so little, but what can I say. Just go and do little, get it out of the way. I figured another day, another time way down the road some place, maybe 40 years from now I'll do something that I get a chance to do what I want to do in keeping with what I can do.
